title: Originally performed as a one woman show, The Whoopi Monologues reima...
transcript: Kerry Washington leads an all star cast of women reciting five distinct character monologues that were originally written and performed by Whoopi Goldberg. And truth be told, when I say Kerry Washington leads the show, while she is definitely the biggest name, she probably has the least to do of the five. The format of the show is essentially an actress comes out, delivers their monologue, then it transitions into the next actress who delivers their monologue, and so on, with Kerry's monologue being the shortest of the five. So if you are going to the show specifically for Kerry Washington, definitely be prepared for that. But truly, all five actresses are giving fantastic performances. You have the always excellent two time Tony winner Kara Young, Tony winner Kecia Lewis, Danielle Pinnock from the TV Show ghosts and Dominique Fishback from the TV Show swarm, each of them bringing a unique energy and flavor to their character. And what's so interesting is that this show was originally a one woman show performed by Whoopi Goldberg. But after seeing this production, it's really hard for me to imagine one actress performing all of these roles. And a lot of that can be contributed to the stellar direction by Whitney White, who is really able to build this sisterhood between these five women. Despite the fact that they really don't interact, besides from the transitions between monologues, there's such a strong sense of community both up on stage and In the room, with the audience very much becoming active participants in these stories. And while I would not call it audience participation per se, if you are sitting anywhere in that first row, definitely expect some interaction. This show feels like a blend between theatre and stand up, with each of the characters fully aware that they are performing for an audience of people, and acknowledging things that are happening in the audience, like people coming in late or a phone going off without ever breaking character. While I would consider the show a comedy, and there are pretty consistent laughs throughout, it does manage to tackle some pretty heavy and serious topics as the show goes on. As I said, these characters feel very real and tangible, and part of that is because they are not perfect. They make mistakes. But the show never looks down on any of these women. It just wants you to see them and to understand them, to experience their joy as well as their pain. And I think the resulting experience is quite beautiful. So if you are looking for a show that is gonna make you laugh, it's gonna make you cry. And performed by five incredible actresses at the top of their game, the Whoopi Monologues is definitely a strong Broadway Ben recommendation.
classificationReason: Creator clearly attended the production and shares specific opinions on all five performers, the format, and the adaptation — a genuine first-hand review.
